features.quote: Rhamphorhynchus (, from Ancient Greek rhamphos meaning "beak" and rhynchus meaning "snout") is a genus of long-tailed pterosaurs in the Jurassic period.

features.claim: Its long tail was stiffened with ligaments.
features.quote: Less specialized than contemporary, short-tailed pterodactyloid pterosaurs such as Pterodactylus, it had a long tail, stiffened with ligaments, which ended in a characteristic soft-tissue tail vane.

features.claim: Its tail ended in a soft-tissue vane.
features.quote: Less specialized than contemporary, short-tailed pterodactyloid pterosaurs such as Pterodactylus, it had a long tail, stiffened with ligaments, which ended in a characteristic soft-tissue tail vane.

features.claim: Its mouth had needle-like teeth angled forward.
features.quote: The mouth of Rhamphorhynchus housed needle-like teeth, which were angled forward, with a curved, sharp, beak-like tip lacking teeth, indicating a diet mainly of fish; indeed, fish and cephalopod remains are frequently found in Rhamphorhynchus abdominal contents, as well as in their coprolites.

features.claim: The tip of its jaws was curved, sharp and beak-like, with no teeth.
features.quote: The mouth of Rhamphorhynchus housed needle-like teeth, which were angled forward, with a curved, sharp, beak-like tip lacking teeth, indicating a diet mainly of fish; indeed, fish and cephalopod remains are frequently found in Rhamphorhynchus abdominal contents, as well as in their coprolites.

features.claim: It had no bony or soft tissue crest on its head.
features.quote: Contrary to a 1927 report by pterosaur researcher Ferdinand Broili, Rhamphorhynchus lacked any bony or soft tissue crest, as seen in several species of contemporary small pterodactyloid pterosaurs.

features.claim: Its teeth intermesh when the jaw is closed.
features.quote: The teeth of Rhamphorhynchus intermesh when the jaw is closed and are suggestive of a piscivorous diet.

features.claim: It had twenty teeth in the upper jaws and fourteen in the lower jaws.
features.quote: There are twenty teeth in the upper jaws and fourteen in the lower jaws.

features.claim: The largest known specimen had an estimated wingspan of 1.8 metres.
features.quote: The largest known specimen of Rhamphorhynchus muensteri (catalog number NHMUK PV OR 37002) has an estimated wingspan of 1.8 metres (5.9 ft).

features.claim: Its body was covered with hairs.
features.quote: Like other pterosaurs, its body was covered with hairs, which suggests it had temperature regulation ('hot-blooded') and a high rate of metabolism.

features.claim: Its feet were broad and large.
features.quote: Its feet are broad and large, being useful for propulsion, and the predicted floating position is adequate by pterosaur standards.

not_this.claim: Old pictures sometimes show a crest on its head, but it had no crest.
not_this.quote: Contrary to a 1927 report by pterosaur researcher Ferdinand Broili, Rhamphorhynchus lacked any bony or soft tissue crest, as seen in several species of contemporary small pterodactyloid pterosaurs.

second_reading.quote: Like several pteranodontians it has hatchet-shaped deltopectoral crests, a short torso and short legs, all features associated with water based launching in pterosaurs.
